notes: Eval 1 runs on a bare Next.js scaffold. Eval 2 runs on a scaffold with jest + @testing-library/jest-dom already installed and a test script pointing at jest. Prompts stay in Thai: they simulate real user input.

evals.name: no-test-infra-at-all
evals.prompt: โปรเจคนี้ยังไม่มี test ไม่มี lint อะไรเลยครับ เดี๋ยวจะทำ jenkins ต่อ ช่วยตั้งให้ครบก่อน
evals.expected_output: Installs vitest (+setup +server-only stub) / eslint / prettier / husky+lint-staged · adds the scripts under the exact names the pipeline calls · vitest emits junit when CI=true and lcov coverage
assertions: package.json has scripts named lint, format:check, test:coverage, build
vitest.config.ts enables the junit reporter only when process.env.CI
The coverage reporter list includes lcov
coverage.include covers every source dir actually present in the project
The server-only alias points at an in-project stub file, not a node_modules path
eslint globalIgnores includes .next/**, out/**, build/**, next-env.d.ts and coverage/**

evals.name: existing-jest-must-ask-before-replacing
evals.prompt: ช่วยตั้ง test ให้ตรงมาตรฐานบริษัทด้วยครับ
evals.expected_output: Detects the existing jest setup, reports what it found, and asks whether to migrate to vitest or keep jest with adjusted reporters — never silently deletes the existing config
assertions: Reports the existing jest installation before acting
Asks the user whether to migrate to vitest or keep jest
Deletes or overwrites no jest config before receiving an answer
If jest is kept, explains that test-results/junit.xml and coverage/lcov.info must still be produced for the pipeline
